<thought>From the measurements we see that the resistance between A and B (151.667 Ω) equals the sum of the measured resistances A‑X1 (6.667 Ω) plus X1‑B (145 Ω). The same holds for the pairs A‑X2 / X2‑B (56.667 Ω + 95 Ω) and A‑X3 / X3‑B (106.667 Ω + 45 Ω). Thus the circuit consists of three parallel branches between terminals A and B, each branch being two resistors in series. No other connections are needed to satisfy the given data, so the minimal topology is:

- Branch 1: A – R1 – X1 – R2 – B with R1 = 6.667 Ω, R2 = 145 Ω  
- Branch 2: A – R3 – X2 – R4 – B with R3 = 56.667 Ω, R4 = 95 Ω  
- Branch 3: A – R5 – X3 – R6 – B with R5 = 106.667 Ω, R6 = 45 Ω  

All measured resistances are reproduced by this network.</thought>
